text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated error rate detected in production after canary deploy. Type: DB schema mismatch during canary migration. Severity P1. Affected endpoints: /v1/ingest, /v1/user/update. See runbook: /runbooks/migrations. Paging: zoe_oncall.

zoe_oncall: I'm up. Grafana shows spike at 1794571200; new deploy to canary cluster at 1794571150. Errors are 4xx/422 and 500s for write paths. Repro locally against canary app + prod DB returns 422: "invalid column type".

rachel_release: Canary config: release 2026-03-15/canary-3 applied to 5% hosts at 1794571150. Migration job `canary_migration_runner` started automatically and reported success on one node but failed on another with exit code 1. Logs: 

```
canary_migration_runner[stdout]: Applying migration 20260315_add_json_field to shard=shard-7
ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}';
Error: column "metadata" already exists (previous partial run)
Exit code: 1
```

zoe_oncall: That partial state would explain mismatch: some app instances expect column metadata to exist, others expect not. Clients hitting different canary pods get different errors. @max_db can you see which shards have partial migration?

max_db: Checking cluster state now. Running `SELECT shard_id, EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='events' AND column_name='metadata') as has_col FROM shard_registry;`

max_db: Results: shard-3: false, shard-7: true, shard-9: false. So only shard-7 has column. That explains inconsistent behavior.

sam_support: We have 12 customer tickets opened in last 10m reporting 422s and duplicated records after retries. One enterprise customer flagged high severity. Notifying them now.

laura_prodeng: Options: 1) Roll forward: ensure all shards get migration quickly (risky during high traffic). 2) Roll back canary to previous image (safer). 3) Feature-flag gate to route traffic away from canary. I'd prefer roll back canary and pause migrations until we enforce per-shard prechecks.

zoe_oncall: Agree roll back canary to stop creating more partial schema states. @rachel_release, can you revert canary at the CDN/loadbalancer level?

rachel_release: Rolling canary back at 1794571275 — removed canary tag from routing. Confirmed: traffic no longer directed to canary pods. However, migration job already touched shard-7; we need to remediate that shard to match others.

max_db: For shard-7 we have two remediation paths: a) revert column (DROP COLUMN) to match others, b) backfill other shards to add column. Dropping column is faster but dangerous if any data was written using metadata. We should check writes to shard-7 between 1794571150-1794571275.

zoe_oncall: Put system into write-protect (read-only) for ingestion endpoints to prevent further divergence. I'll flip API gateway to return 503 for write endpoints at 1794571290.

sam_support: Updating customers: "We detected a canary migration inconsistency affecting some write requests. We have paused writes and are working on remediation. Will share ETA in 30 mins."

max_db: Querying writes: `SELECT count(*) FROM events WHERE updated_at BETWEEN to_timestamp(1794571150) AND to_timestamp(1794571275) AND shard='shard-7';` -> 4,812 rows. Some have non-empty metadata values set by canary code.

laura_prodeng: Given that data exists on shard-7, better to add column to other shards rather than drop it. We can sequence this carefully: add column with default NULL and backfill asynchronously from an S3 dump of shard-7, but that's slower. Is there a way to make app tolerant?

rachel_release: We can flip feature flag `use_metadata_field` to false so app doesn't write to metadata even if column exists. That avoids further writes to metadata while we reconcile. I'll flip it now.

rachel_release: Flag set to false at 1794571322. Canary pods still had column but should stop writing to it.

zoe_oncall: Initiating targeted schema roll forward for non-impacted shards at low QPS windows. Schedule: add column on shard-3 and shard-9 with `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN metadata JSONB` but with `LOCK` minimization: use `ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT '{}'` in two steps to avoid long exclusive locks. I'll coordinate with @max_db.

max_db: On it. Running `ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN metadata JSONB;` on shard-3 in a connection with statement_timeout=5min and low concurrency. If we see lock waits above 30s we'll pause. Executed at 1794571360.

max_db: Shard-3 column added successfully at 1794571390. Shard-9 started at 1794571400.

sam_support: Customers acknowledged the pause and appreciate the proactive updates. One customer requested a rollback instead of forward migration; they prefer schema parity over changes.

laura_prodeng: We should prefer forward migration to restore parity quickly. Once shard-9 completes, we can resume writes in a constrained mode and run reconciliation to detect duplicates/invalid metadata.

max_db: Shard-9 column added at 1794571445. Backfill plan: run idempotent reconciliation job that looks for events with metadata only on shard-7 and copy sanitized metadata to other shards where missing. Starting backfill in 1,000-row batches.

zoe_oncall: Before resuming full writes, we'll enable a soft throttle at 20% QPS and increase retry backoff client-side. Applying throttle at API gateway now (1794571488).

rachel_release: I'll monitor application logs for schema-related exceptions. No new 422s on hosts after canary rollback and flags changed.

max_db: Backfill progress: batch 1 ok (1,000 rows), batch 2 ok, batch 3 had 7 conflicts due to existing differing metadata; those rows flagged for manual review. So far processed 3,000/4,812 rows.

sam_support: Ticket update: told customers we'll be removing write freeze in 45-60 mins assuming backfill completes and no regressions. One customer asked for a postmortem.

laura_prodeng: Action items for postmortem (note): - Prevent auto-running migrations during canary; require manual approval. - Add per-shard precheck to migration runner. - Add canary guard to stop feature flag flip that causes schema writes until migration fully completes.

zoe_oncall: Bringing system back to degraded write mode at 1794571520: writes allowed at 25% QPS, stricter client retries. Monitoring.

max_db: Backfill finished at 1794571548. 4,812 rows processed, 7 manual-conflict rows triaged and fixed. No data loss observed.

rachel_release: Canary rollback complete, schema parity restored. Removing throttles slowly.

sam_support: Sent second update to customers: "Write operations restored in degraded mode; ongoing reconciliation completed. Postmortem forthcoming." No new high-severity tickets.

zoe_oncall: Error rate returned to baseline by 1794571558. Summarizing: root cause partial schema application on shard-7 during automated canary migration; cause: migration tool allowed partial success on subset of shards. Mitigations: rolled back canary, feature flag off, paused writes, added columns to other shards, backfilled, resumed degraded writes.

zoe_oncall: Handing off to next oncall @nate_next_oncall at 1794571560. Please watch for late-arriving errors and coordinate postmortem.

nate_next_oncall: Taking over. I'll coordinate the follow-ups: postmortem, migration control changes, and customer incident note.

incident-bot: Incident downgraded to P2 at 1794571560 (system stable; ongoing action items).
